deficiencies.description: The rewrite states that death can occur 'when the tumour occurs in a meningioma', treating a meningioma as an anatomical location where a tumour arises rather than as the tumour itself.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: Only 10% of these deaths, generally, if they're occurring in things like the meningioma that I was telling you about or in the liver.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: when the tumour occurs in a meningioma or in the liver
deficiencies.caseForForbidden: A meningioma is a tumour of the meninges rather than a bodily site in which a tumour can occur, so assigning 'meningioma' the role of an anatomical site distorts the medical terminology.
deficiencies.caseForAllowed: The lecturer said 'if they're occurring in things like the meningioma', and the rewrite simply interpreted the pronoun 'they' as referring to tumours.

considerations.sourcePassage: Things like obstruction of the bile ducts in the liver interferes with digestion.
considerations.reason: The introductory sentence 'Other effects depend on the site' was added to structure the paragraph following the lecturer's discussion of different anatomical settings, serving as a stylistic transition rather than an unsourced factual claim.

considerations.sourcePassage: And also this competition with the normal, if you have a tumor that is occurring in some of the blood compartments, the hematopoietic stem cells that are there, these will interfere.
considerations.reason: The rewrite's phrasing 'Competition with normal tissue is also a factor' accurately expresses the meaning of the lecturer's incomplete phrasing 'competition with the normal' in the context of haematopoietic stem cells.

considerations.sourcePassage: you saw that enormous cauliflower structure within the colon
considerations.reason: Changing 'cauliflower structure' to 'cauliflower-like structure seen within the colon' is an allowed stylistic rewording referring to the same visual feature previously shown.
